rows.why: S1 is about the CSV's overall layout. Item 3 (the header columns and their order) is the closest single match, though items 1 (BOM), 5 (row order) and 2 (CRLF) each cover one of its other clauses. The run shows the exact header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created'. The other runs agree too: a leading U+FEFF, rows sorted by creation time then id, and CRLF after every row including the last.

Item 6 asks how the creation time is formatted, which is the main formatting question in S2. S2 wants the UTC date as 'YYYY-MM-DD', but the run writes the full toISOString() value, e.g. '2009-02-13T23:31:30.123Z'. The runs also write the status as 'open' rather than 'Open', and no list item asks about how status is displayed. Item 8 (missing title written as an empty field) agrees, but it only covers one clause.
Item 4 asks what an empty list produces. The run returns the BOM plus the header line and its CRLF, with no data rows, which is exactly what S3 expects.

Item 7 asks when and how fields are quoted. Its pick quotes only when a field contains a comma, quote, CR or LF. S4 also requires quoting a title that starts or ends with a space, and the pick as written leaves those unquoted.
No item asks about defusing titles that start like a formula (prefixing '=', '+', '-', '@', tab or CR with a single quote). Item 7 covers quoting, which is a different behaviour.

Item 12 asks the general question of what happens when a requisition is invalid: fail the whole build or skip the row. Items 9, 10 and 11 each cover one specific reason. The runs throw Errors that name the requisition id (e.g. 'Requisition bad has an unknown status "nope"'), which matches S6. No item or run covers S6's invalid creation time case.
